price_value.rationale: The current $19,000 bid is below the $24,973-$31,074 fair-value band, but a no-reserve BaT car will likely finish near the low end of that band. Three prior owners and an unexplained dealer reacquisition offset the value; there are no known-work items.

mission_fit.rationale: Porsche is on the active exclusion list and the Cayman is deferred to 2027-28. The car would work as a manual fun daily, but as a future-keeper it conflicts with the current cash-preservation and accelerated-bridge plan, and owners are above the two-owner preference.

logistics.rationale: North Salem, NY is far from Pacific Grove. An appointment viewing on 11/6 and BaT shipping help, but the window for a mobile PPI before the 11/7 close is very tight. CA registration looks feasible with stock powertrain.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A typical base 2.7 manual in black over Stone Grey. The manual and Cayman S wheels are modest pluses, offset by aftermarket springs and clear markers. No rare colour or option set.

Down: over-rev counts in ranges 4-6, an active AOS or RMS leak, or a slipping clutch.

evidence.mission_note: A base 2.7 manual Cayman is a coherent future-keeper, but Porsche is currently excluded and deferred to 2027-28. Buying now conflicts with the accelerated-bridge, cash-preserving plan built around an MX-5 RF or Z3. It is attractive only as a keeper, not as the current bridge.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2007 Cayman 2.7 coupe, the title is stated as clean New Jersey, the Carfax snapshot reports no accidents, and the car's 2021 BaT sale at $27,000 is traceable. Substantial 2026 preparation is described (water pump, thermostat, coolant flush, ignition, belt, transaxle service, front brakes), but none of it was examined as an invoice here. The DME over-rev report and AOS history are absent. Observed issues are three prior Carfax owners plus an unexplained dealer reacquisition, and oily grime on the sump area in the underside photo, whose source is undetermined. Tires carry 2021/2022 codes and are within the six-year window, so no known-work items are established. The $19,000 bid sits below the $24,973-$31,074 fair-value band two days before a no-reserve close, so the hammer is likely to rise. The model itself sits on Jason's current exclusion list and is deferred to 2027-28.
